text.p: Russian ultra-nationalist leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky arrived in Tripoli for talks with Libyan officials, the Libyan news agency JANA reported on Tuesday.
On his arrival on Monday night, the leader of the Russian Liberal Democratic Party condemned the United Nations Security Council sanctions imposed on Libya since 1992 over the Lockerbie affair.
"(Zhirinovsky) renewed the stand and the solidarity of his country with the Great Jamahiriya (Libya) in its confrontation against the injust sanctions imposed on it," JANA, monitored in Tunis, said.
"This visit comes within the framework of supporting and boosting the friendship and cooperation relations between the Great Jamahiriya and Russia," it also quoted him as saying.
Libya is under U.N. sanctions for failing to hand over to the United States or Britain two Libyan suspects in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, that killed 270 people.
Zhirinovsky visited Libya in March 1996 and met Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.
